title: What is on the SD card

steps.title: A GPT disk where programs find their part by name
steps.body:
The card carries a GPT (GUID Partition Table) written by `scripts/image.sh`. The strip at the top shows the first 18 MiB to scale, the five cards show each partition, and the bottom shows what is inside `rootfs`.

The Boot ROM and BL2 look partitions up by NAME and TYPE GUID, never by position, so the offsets are ours to choose.

steps.title: Most of the early disk is empty
steps.body:
From the left: the GPT itself, the two small `fsbla` partitions just after 1 MiB, the 4 MiB `fip` partition ending at 5.5 MiB, `u-boot-env` at 9 MiB, and `rootfs` from 16 MiB to the end of the card.

The gaps marked unused hold nothing. Because the ROM and BL2 look partitions up by name and type, the offsets are only a choice made by `scripts/image.sh`.

steps.title: fsbla1 and fsbla2 hold two copies of BL2
steps.body:
Each is 256 KiB and holds `tf-a-stm32mp257f-dk.stm32` (BL2, 175,080 bytes in this build), starting at sectors 2048 and 2560. The Boot ROM reads `fsbla1` and falls back to `fsbla2` when the first image is bad.

If neither is named correctly, the ROM has nothing to start and the board never boots from the card.

steps.title: fip holds everything BL2 loads next
steps.body:
The 4 MiB partition at sector 3072 has TYPE GUID `19D5DF83-11B0-457B-BE2C-7559C13142A5` and holds `fip.bin`: BL31, OP-TEE, U-Boot, the DDR firmware and DTBs (2.0 MB in this build). A FIP is the packed firmware file.

BL2 finds it by that GUID or by the name `fip`, so the partition can sit anywhere.

steps.title: u-boot-env keeps U-Boot's saved settings
steps.body:
This 512 KiB partition at sector 18432 is read by U-Boot and holds the U-Boot environment, two copies at the end of the partition.

U-Boot finds it by partition name (`u-boot,mmc-env-partition`); the raw offsets `0x900000` and `0x940000` are only a fallback.

steps.title: rootfs is the only partition Linux uses
steps.body:
The ext4 partition (label `rootfs`) starts at sector 32768 and takes the rest of the card. U-Boot reads the kernel from it, then Linux mounts it as `/`.

It is the only partition with the GPT 'bootable' flag, which is how U-Boot knows where to look.

steps.title: The kernel and its device tree live inside rootfs
steps.body:
`/boot/Image` is the kernel, `/boot/stm32mp257f-dk-primer.dtb` its device tree, and `/lib/modules/6.18.58-custom/…` holds the drivers built as modules. The rest is the distribution (`/sbin/init`, `/usr`, `/home`).

The PARTUUID is the partition's unique ID, which the kernel command line uses to find the root.

steps.title: extlinux.conf tells U-Boot what to start
steps.body:
U-Boot reads this small file: `LINUX` names the kernel, `FDT` the device tree, and `APPEND` the kernel command line. That line has `root=PARTUUID=…`, `console=ttySTM0,115200`, `rootwait` (wait for the SD card to appear) and `rw` (mount read-write).

Without the file U-Boot finds nothing to boot.

steps.title: Takeaway: each stage finds its part in a different way
steps.body:
The ROM looks for the partition named `fsbla1`, then `fsbla2`. BL2 looks for the FIP TYPE GUID, or the name `fip`. U-Boot scans the partition with the 'bootable' flag (GPT attribute bit 2) first.

Linux uses `root=PARTUUID=…`, which finds `rootfs` on any `mmcblk` number: the SD card is not always `mmcblk0`.
